title: Eventstream reprocess orchestration for console usage analytics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an orchestration service + safe runner to reprocess historical console event streams into the usage analytics warehouse. The goal is a repeatable, idempotent, and observable pipeline that supports: per-tenant partial replays, schema evolution handling, out-of-order events, and incremental checkpointing so large backfills do not block production traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Run full reprocess of 3 months of console events for a single tenant with end-to-end validated counts vs source (<=1% delta)
Support point-in-time replay: ability to start from event timestamp or checkpoint token
Idempotency guarantee: reprocessing same range twice produces no duplicate rows in warehouse
Monitoring: per-job metrics exported (records_processed, records_skipped, error_rate, lag_seconds) and visible in Console Analytics dashboard
Failure recovery: job resumes from last committed checkpoint after worker restart without manual intervention
implementation_steps: Design coordinator API: create job, list jobs, pause/resume, cancel
Define checkpoint format and durable storage (S3 + Dynamo/Consul) for offsets and watermark metadata
Implement worker that reads compressed event parquet from archival store, applies transform logic, and writes deduped output to staging tables
Add idempotent write mode to warehouse load (MERGE on dedupe key and event_offset)
Wire coordinator and workers into existing infra (k8s cron/Job controller + autoscaling group) and create Helm chart
Integrate job-level tracing and logs into Console Observability (span per shard + sampling)
Create test harness to run small-scale replays against test dataset and compare with golden queries
Run canary backfill for non-critical tenant and validate metrics/delta before scaling
decisions: Use archival S3 as the canonical source for replays to avoid impacting live Kafka clusters
Checkpoint metadata stored in a small Dynamo table keyed by job_id and tenant_id for fast leader election
Workers will perform transforms using the existing analytics transform library (java/scalding -> migrated to Golang shim) to reuse validation logic
Write into staging parquet partitions and then run idempotent MERGE into Redshift/Snowflake via existing ingestion job to leverage existing lineage and BI access
tradeoffs: Choosing S3 reads reduces load on Kafka but increases complexity around partition discovery and small-file handling
Dynamo for checkpoints is fast and simple but requires applying an additional IAM policy and monitoring for hot keys
Idempotent MERGE increases warehouse CPU costs during backfills compared to append-only loads but avoids downstream duplicate handling complexity
blockers: Finalizing IAM roles for the reprocess service to grant read access to archival buckets (security team review pending)
Need updated schema migration mapping from Research to handle new event fields introduced in 2025.11
Pending approval for a temporary increase in Redshift concurrency quota during backfills
